biography: Edson Mori's journey began not on asphalt, but on the dusty karting tracks of São Paulo. Growing up near Interlagos, the roar of engines was his lullaby. His father, a mechanic with a passion for motorsport, introduced him to karting at the age of 8. Edson wasn't immediately a prodigy. He lacked the raw aggression of some of his peers, but his meticulous approach and unwavering focus set him apart. A defining moment came at the Brazilian National Karting Championship in 2018. Down on power, Edson strategically managed his tires and capitalized on others' mistakes, climbing from 15th to secure a podium finish. This calculating drive earned him the attention of Kart 4, a team known for nurturing young talent. Now, at 22, Edson is a rising star in the Formula Sudamericana series, steadily honing his skills with the goal of reaching Formula 3.
drivingStyle: Mori's driving style is characterized by his methodical approach. He's not one for flamboyant overtaking maneuvers or last-minute dives. Instead, he meticulously analyzes track conditions, tire wear, and competitor behavior. He prefers to build momentum throughout a race, patiently waiting for the opportune moment to strike. His tire management is exceptional, often allowing him to push harder in the final stages of a race when others are struggling. He handles pressure with remarkable composure, rarely making rash decisions even in high-stakes situations.

careerHighlight: Winning the 2021 Formula Sudamericana race at Curitiba after starting from 8th on the grid. He conserved his tires expertly and overtook three cars in the final two laps.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2022 Buenos Aires Formula Sudamericana race due to a rare lapse in concentration. The incident cost him valuable championship points.
